extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in humor, communication, and social/psychological uses of self-deprecation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and descriptive criteria about what self-deprecation is, why people use it, and how it functions in social interaction, comedy, and social media. Useful for writers, performers, or communicators considering self-deprecating remarks or analysing their effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of self-deprecation
rubrics_metrics.description: The act of reprimanding oneself by belittling, undervaluing, disparaging oneself, or being excessively modest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-deprecation can be used to make complaints, express modesty, invoke desired reactions, or add humour. This is the baseline definition to determine whether a remark counts as self-deprecating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-defence / Stoic response
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of self-deprecation as a tactic to respond to insults: join in by insulting oneself to remove the sting of the original insult.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: According to Stoic recommendation, self-insulting in response to an insult can (a) remove emotional impact, (b) disappoint the attacker by showing no upset, and (c) reduce future attempts to wound. Useful as a deliberate defensive strategy; anti-pattern is reacting with visible hurt or retaliatory anger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Likeability through flaw-display
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-deprecation allows individuals to appear more likable by showing flaws and deflecting praise; people prefer self-criticism over being criticized by others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because boasting is often perceived negatively, presenting oneself negatively can reduce perceptions of arrogance. High-status individuals (wealthy, accomplished, attractive) may be perceived more positively if they highlight personal flaws and downplay successes. Use when aiming to increase approachability or reduce perceived threat to others' self-concept; be mindful of authenticity and not eroding respect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Politeness and cultural norms (British/traditional contexts)
rubrics_metrics.description: In traditional British English culture and similar contexts, self-deprecation is considered an element of modesty and politeness, contrasted with North American self-confidence norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In cultures where 'blowing one's own trumpet' is frowned upon (e.g., UK, Ireland, Australia, New Zealand), self-belittling signals putting others first and is seen as polite. Use to conform to modesty norms; avoid overt self-promotion in these contexts. Anti-pattern: visible boasting where modesty is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedic technique and persona-building
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-deprecation is a major component of many comedians' styles and can be used as a comedic device or persona (examples include Rodney Dangerfield, Woody Allen, Nathan Fielder, Don Knotts, Joan Rivers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a comedic tool, self-deprecation can generate laughs by exposing vulnerabilities, creating contrast, or establishing a relatable persona. Use in timing, setup/punchline structures, or as recurring character trait. Beware of overuse that blunts comedic impact or undermines the performer's credibility (unless the persona requires it).

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media usage and coping function
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-deprecating humor is popular on platforms like Instagram, X, and TikTok—especially among Gen Z and millennials—often used to cope with stress, mental-health struggles, or social pressure to appear perfect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common themes include 'feeling dead inside' or joking about mental illness; such posts can build solidarity and increase engagement because they normalize imperfection. Platform norms favor modesty over boasting; users often employ self-deprecating hashtags to appear less arrogant. Caution: these posts can trivialize serious issues or attract criticism if perceived as attention-seeking or insensitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential negative effects and authority erosion
rubrics_metrics.description: Although self-deprecation can increase likability, researchers note it can lead individuals to feel they don't deserve praise and can undermine their authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use self-deprecation judiciously: excessive or frequent self-belittling may harm self-esteem, reduce perceived competence, or weaken leadership/authority. Balance self-deprecating remarks with evidence of competence where appropriate; avoid using self-deprecation in contexts where authority and confidence are required.
